title: Filmmaking Execution Path
purpose: Help users learn filmmaking by creating short, finished visual scenes instead of passively studying theory.
core_output: A finished short scene, video, storyboard, trailer, documentary clip, or edited sequence.

30_second_start: Choose one emotion for a scene.
3_minute_start: Record a 10-second shot showing one emotion.
Create a 3-shot storyboard: wide, medium, close-up.
Find one movie scene and note one camera angle.
10_minute_build: Shoot a 15-second scene with beginning, middle, and end.
Create a one-minute mood trailer using phone footage.

phases.name: Shoot One Emotion
phases.objective: Create a tiny finished scene fast.
phases.checkpoint: User has one filmed clip that communicates an emotion.

phases.name: Control Shots
phases.objective: Use framing and shot choice intentionally.
phases.checkpoint: User can explain why each shot exists.

phases.name: Edit for Feeling
phases.objective: Learn pacing and emotion through cuts.
phases.checkpoint: User has an edited sequence with intentional pacing.

phases.name: Sound + Atmosphere
phases.checkpoint: User compares two audio versions and explains the difference.

phases.name: Publishable Short
phases.objective: Finish and share a small complete film artifact.
phases.checkpoint: User has a finished video file or shareable link.

modalities.hands_on: Shoot or edit before watching tutorials.
modalities.visual: Use storyboards, reference frames, and shot maps.
modalities.audio: Describe the scene out loud before filming.
modalities.walking: Walk and brainstorm the scene's emotion or story beat.
modalities.music_supported: Pick a track first and edit to its energy.
modalities.reading: Read one tiny film concept and apply it in the next shot.

adaptive_rules.action: Only capture one shot or storyboard one frame.
Offer a 30-minute shoot/edit sprint with a stopping checkpoint.
Remove equipment complexity. Use phone-only filming.
Use a favorite movie style or recreate a scene.

outside_app_uses: Turn school material into a short film assignment.
